chapter: Southern Illinois roadhouse and St. Louis
title: Dropping the clarinet for alto sax; still owing Doc Moon
summary: Joe fell in love with the alto sax and let his clarinet go, still owing Doc Moon ninety dollars and hoping to find a circus in Billboard.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Did you quit playing the clarinet, or did you keep playing the two of them?
No, I practically dropped the clarinet.
Oh, that's interesting. I never thought of that.
Yes, I practically got off the clarinet. But to tell you the truth, I fell in love with the saxophone. At that time, people loved saxophone.
Barney said the same thing, but he said he never could play it, so he didn't...
He had to play the tenor in Joe Oliver's band, I think, but he didn't like to play it -- but you're the opposite.

Yes, I just loved the alto saxophone. And I can't remember what happened to my clarinet, whether I sold it or lost it or gave it away. I really don't know what happened to it. Anyway, my saxophone still wasn't paid for with Doc Moon.
No. I had to keep making payments. I think I still owed him ninety dollars.
You must have missed a heck of a lot of payments!

Every time he'd wanted to take off the two dollars, I said, "Hey, Doc, I need that two dollars." He said, "Okay, I'll take it out next week." Kept putting it off. But he never forgot I owed him ninety dollars, and I never forgot it either, for that matter. So I told Charlie Berger, this gangster, "I'd like to stay here and work." Because that's when I figured I want to settle down right here and try and get me a Billboard... That advertised all the circuses that was traveling, and that's the magazine you picked up if you wanted a job -- the Billboard Magazine.
